model.title: Model
model.subtitle: attention_ablation
model.doc: The model's width, vocabulary, residual algebra and initialization: the settings every layer reads.

fields.doc: The width of the residual stream.
The vocabulary's size: the embedding's rows and the head's outputs.
The residual algebra: what `[f]` means. none is x + f(x).
How weight matrices start.

node:n.0.title: Token embedding
node:n.0.subtitle: embed
node:n.0.doc:
The token embedding: token ids to the stream, by a table of `vocab_size` rows
of `d_model`. A model starts with one, and a tied head and nextn read the table
of its first. Under a residual algebra that widens the stream, it returns that
many copies of the embedding.

fields.doc: Learned absolute positions (GPT-2): a table of this many, added to the embedding; None: none.
Multiply the embedding by sqrt(d_model) (Gemma).
A norm of the embedding, after the scale and before positions are added (Inkling); nextn reads the embedding normalized too.
Dropout rate of the embedding, in training.

node:n.1.title: Repeat
node:n.1.subtitle: ×12
node:n.1.doc: `body^n`: n copies of the body in sequence, each with its own parameters.

fields.doc: How many fresh copies of the body run in sequence.

node:n.1.0.0.0.0.title: RMSNorm
node:n.1.0.0.0.0.subtitle: rmsnorm · norm
node:n.1.0.0.0.0.doc:
Layer normalization (Ba et al., 2016) or RMSNorm (Zhang & Sennrich, 2019).

``layernorm`` subtracts the mean over the width and divides by the standard
deviation; ``rmsnorm`` only divides by the root mean square. Then each multiplies
by a learned gain per channel (`affine`) and adds a learned bias (`bias`). A norm
is a layer, ``[norm attn]``, and a setting of layers that normalize something of
their own, as ``gqa(qk_norm=rmsnorm)``.

fields.doc: Added to the variance (rmsnorm: mean square) before its root.
A learned gain per channel, the norm's scale.
A learned bias per channel, added last (GPT-2's layernorms).
The gain as 1 + w, with w learned from 0 (Gemma, Qwen3-Next).
Where the gain starts: 1 / sqrt(layers) is Trinity's depth-scaled sandwich norm, [norm attn norm(gain_init=layers ^ -0.5)].
Multiply by the gain before normalizing, norm(w * x), not after (Muse Spark).

node:n.1.0.0.0.1.title: Grouped-query attention
node:n.1.0.0.0.1.subtitle: gqa · attn
node:n.1.0.0.0.1.doc:
Grouped-query attention; MHA when num_kv_heads == num_heads, MQA when it is 1.

Causal softmax attention (Vaswani et al., 2017) of `num_heads` query heads and
`num_kv_heads` key and value heads, each shared by a group of
``num_heads / num_kv_heads`` query heads (Ainslie et al., 2023):
``gqa(num_heads=32, num_kv_heads=8, rope=rope())``.

Ports: ``v`` exports the value heads, or imports them for value-residual mixing
(ResFormer); ``kv`` exports keys and values, or imports them instead of computing
its own (cross-layer KV sharing, YOCO / CLA); ``index`` shares the indexer's top-k.

fields.doc: query heads
key and value heads, each shared by a group of query heads
dims of each head; None -> width // num_heads
Dims of each value head; None -> head_dim (MiMo-V2: 128 against 192).
Biases on the projections of the input: q, k, v and the gate (GPT-2, Qwen2).
A bias on the output projection; None -> bias (GPT-2). Qwen2 has none.
Make q, k and v with one projection and split it, instead of one projection each: the same function and init, held as one matrix (GPT-2, MiMo-V2.6-Pro).

qk_norm over all the heads together: one norm of the queries' num_heads * head_dim channels and one of the keys', each with a gain per channel, before they split into heads (MiniMax-M2, OLMo 2). Without qk_norm it does nothing.
Rotary embedding of q and k; None: no positions.
Theta, the base of the frequencies (Llama 3: 500000).
Partial rotary: only this fraction of each head's dims is rotated, the first ones, in whole pairs (GLM, Qwen3-Next).
Which rotated dims pair up: "half" rotates dim i with i + dims / 2 (GPT-NeoX, Llama), "interleaved" rotates dim 2i with 2i + 1 (GPT-J, Cohere).
Context extension; None: none.

Queries scaled by (1 + n / power_scale_length) ** power_scale at their position n, counted from 1, so that attention without RoPE stays sharp at long range (Beam's global layers); None: no scaling. It scales q, so every attention method runs it.
Where the queries' scale reaches 2 ** power_scale.
Causal depthwise conv on keys and values, of this many taps, added to them: k + conv(k) (Inkling); None: none.

How a layer that reads the v port mixes its values v1 into its own v, as a v + b v1 starting from a = b = 0.5: "fixed" keeps a and b (ResFormer's code), "learned" learns both (Learnable-ResFormer), "convex" learns a, with b = 1 - a.
Each query attends to this many keys: itself and those just before it (local attention). None: every key before it.
Dropout rate of the attention probabilities, in training; it needs all t by t of them, so it runs under methods.attention xla or auto alone.
Dropout rate of the output, in training.
Elementwise gate act(W_g x) on each head's output, before the output projection (Qwen3-Next's gated attention; the activation is gate_activation).
One gate value per head instead (Laguna).

fields.type: relu | relu2 | gelu | gelu_tanh | swish | sigmoid | tanh | softplus | situ | quick_gelu
fields.doc: Of the gate (Laguna: softplus).
A learned bias per head on the gate, before its activation, shared by the head's dims and starting at 0 (Beam).
A norm of each head's output, before the gate (Muse); None: none.
Norm of each query and key head, before RoPE (Qwen3); gqa's qk_norm_all_heads makes it one of all the heads together. None: none.
Soft-capping of the logits, softcap * tanh(logits / softcap) (Gemma 2); None: none.
A learned sink logit per head, in every query's softmax beside its keys', that takes a share of the attention and gives no value (gpt-oss).
The logits' scale. None -> head_dim ** -0.5 (MLA: of qk_nope_head_dim + qk_rope_head_dim); YaRN with attention_factor_on=softmax multiplies it by attention_factor ** 2.

Logits scaled by 1 + log_scale * ln(max(n / log_scale_floor, 1)) at the query's position n, counted from 1, so that attention stays sharp at long range (Inkling); None: no scaling. It runs under methods.attention xla or auto alone. Not Llama 4's temperature tuning, 1 + s * ln(1 + floor(position / floor)): a step function, on its NoPE layers.
Positions up to this one keep their logits' scale.
A learned relative position bias.
A lightning indexer that picks the keys each query attends to; None: all of them.

node:n.1.0.1.0.1.title: Gated feed-forward
node:n.1.0.1.0.1.subtitle: gated_mlp · ffn
node:n.1.0.1.0.1.doc:
A dense MLP, ``mlp``, or a gated one, ``gated_mlp`` (GLU variants; Shazeer,
2020): ``down(act(up(x)))``, or ``down(act(gate(x)) * up(x))``. SwiGLU is
``gated_mlp(activation=swish)``. It is also the shape of an MoE's experts
(`MoEConfig.expert`).

fields.doc: Hidden units: the output width of up (and of gate).

fields.type: relu | relu2 | gelu | gelu_tanh | swish | sigmoid | tanh | softplus | situ | quick_gelu
fields.doc: Of the hidden units, or of the gate when gated.
Dropout rate of the output, in training.
Biases on the up, gate and down projections.
Clamped SwiGLU: the gate input is capped at limit, the up branch at +-limit (gpt-oss, DeepSeek-V4); None: no clamp.
Soft-capping of the up branch, cap * tanh(up / cap) (Kimi K3); None: none.
Added to a gated MLP's up branch after it is clipped: gpt-oss's up + 1.

node:n.3.title: Output head
node:n.3.subtitle: head
node:n.3.doc:
The language-model head: the stream to logits over the vocabulary,
``softcap(x W + b)``. Every head is an output of the model; nothing follows one
but a tap read, as a multi-token prediction module does (`NextNConfig`).

fields.doc: Use the model's first embedding table, transposed, as W.
A learned bias per token of the vocabulary.
Soft-capping of the logits, softcap * tanh(logits / softcap) (Gemma 2); None: none.

setting:optimizer.title: Optimizer
setting:optimizer.subtitle: adamw
setting:optimizer.doc:
AdamW (Loshchilov & Hutter, 2019), by optax. Weight decay applies to matrices
and stacks of them, not to norm scales, biases, other vectors or what a module
names in `no_weight_decay`.

fields.doc: the peak learning rate, which the schedule scales
the decay of the first moment, the gradients' average
the decay of the second moment, the squared gradients' average
added to the second moment's square root, against zero
decoupled, of the matrices, times the learning rate

setting:schedule.title: Schedule
setting:schedule.subtitle: wsd
setting:schedule.doc:
Warmup-stable-decay (Hu et al., 2024): warmup, the peak, then a cooldown to
`final` times the peak over the last `decay` of the steps. Checkpoints from the
stable phase can be cooled down later, to study several run lengths at once.

fields.doc: steps of linear warmup, or a share of them below 1
The share of the steps the cooldown takes, rounded to a number of steps.
the multiplier at the last step: a fraction of the peak

fields.type: linear | sqrt | cosine | exp | geometric | constant
fields.doc: the cooldown's curve

setting:data.title: Data
setting:data.subtitle: mix
setting:data.doc:
Sources in proportion to their weights, in every batch: a batch's rows are
dealt out by the weights, normalized, the largest remainders first. It is written
as a weighted sum, ``0.7 * web + 0.3 * code``; ``web + code`` is an even mix.
A source whose weight leaves it no row of a batch is an error.

fields.doc: the sources and their weights, as written
fields.value: (Weighted(weight=0.8, source=TextConfig(type='text', path='data/fineweb-edu/*.parquet', column='text', bos=True, eos=True, split=(0.0, 0.999))), Weighted(weight=0.2, source=TextConfig(type='text', path='data/stack-edu/*.parquet', column='content', bos=True, eos=True, split=(0.0, 1.0))))

setting:tokenizer.title: Tokenizer
setting:tokenizer.subtitle: tokenizer
setting:tokenizer.doc:
A Hugging Face tokenizer: a Hub repo or a `tokenizer.json`, run by gigatoken,
or by Hugging Face's tokenizers where gigatoken cannot run it (SmolLM2's, or one
that is not BPE). `text` and `chat` data need one.

Special tokens written in documents stay text, as tiktoken's `encode_ordinary`
keeps them: a web page that mentions `<|endoftext|>` does not end there. Only
`bos`, `eos` and chat templates put them in.

fields.doc: "gpt2", "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B", or a path to a tokenizer.json
The token a document starts with, where its source sets `bos`; Llama 3's is "<|begin_of_text|>".
The token a document ends with, where its source sets `eos`; Llama 3's is "<|end_of_text|>".
Special tokens after the vocabulary, for a template it lacks: GPT-2's 50257 tokens padded to 50304 leave room for ["<|im_start|>", "<|im_end|>"].

setting:packing.title: Packing
setting:packing.subtitle: best_fit
setting:packing.doc:
Best-fit decreasing (Ding et al., 2024): the longest documents first, each into
the open row that it leaves least room in. Nearly no padding, and documents are
only cut when they are longer than a row, into pieces that fill gaps.

fields.doc: positions start at every document, attention within it
A document longer than a row: dropped, truncated to a row, or split into pieces that fill gaps.
The most documents and pieces of them in a row, for attention kernels that take a fixed number of them. None: as many as fit.
longest first; false keeps the shuffled order (online best fit)
about how many tokens of documents pack together

setting:loss.title: Loss
setting:loss.subtitle: loss
setting:loss.doc:
The loss a run minimizes: the cross-entropy of the first head, plus `z` times
its z-loss, plus `mtp` times the mean cross-entropy of the heads after it, each of
which predicts one token further ahead for every `nextn` before it. The losses
layers report, as an MoE's balance loss, add with the weights set on the layer.

fields.doc: weight of the z-loss, log(Z)^2 of the first head (PaLM: 1e-4)
Weight of the mean loss of the heads that predict further ahead (DeepSeek-V3).

setting:eval.title: Eval
setting:eval.subtitle: eval
setting:eval.doc:
Held-out loss every `every` steps and after the last, over the same `batches`
batches of `data` each time: the first head's mean cross-entropy over their
targets, logged as `eval_loss`, and with a `tokenizer`, its bits per byte,
`eval_bpb`. A batch has the run's `batch` rows of `seq_len` tokens.

Bits per byte compare across tokenizers: the targets' nats over their bytes of
text, in bits. A special token stands for no text, so they leave it out.

A run takes a list of them, a held-out set each under a name of its own, which
its metrics start with: `eval = [eval(name="web", data=web(split=[0.99, 1])),
eval(name="code", data=code(split=[0.99, 1]))]` logs `web_loss`, `web_bpb`,
`code_loss` and `code_bpb`.

Held-out batches are a stream of their own seed, not other documents: hold
documents out of training by their hash, as `eval(data=web(split=[0.99, 1]))`
beside `data = web(split=[0, 0.99])`.

fields.doc: What its metrics' names start with: eval_loss, eval_bpb.
a source or a mixture, as `data` takes
a glob of Parquet files, relative to the working directory
the column that holds each document's text
start every document with the tokenizer's `bos`
end it with its `eos`, so that the model learns where text ends
The documents whose hash falls in [start, end): [0.99, 1] is a 1% held out.
steps between evaluations
batches an evaluation reads, the same ones each time

setting:checkpoint.title: Checkpoint
setting:checkpoint.subtitle: checkpoint
setting:checkpoint.doc:
Model and optimizer state, saved in the run's directory every `every` steps, at
the end, and at the step a run stops at early (as at SIGTERM). A run that finds a
checkpoint there resumes from the latest one, and its data from the batch after.

Every process of a job saves its part, so the run's directory must be one that
every node sees. A run resumes only with the methods it was saved with where they
lay out its state: `repeat`, a circular pipeline's `rounds` and an uneven
pipeline's `stages`.

fields.doc: steps between saves
the most recent checkpoints to keep

setting:log.title: Log
setting:log.subtitle: log
setting:log.doc:
Training metrics every `every` steps and after the last, to the console and to
the run's metrics.jsonl, and to each of `trackers`: the loss and its terms,
`grad_norm`, `lr`, `tokens`, `tokens_per_s`, `mfu` on devices whose peak FLOPs
bux knows, the time a step takes and where the host spends it, and the device's
memory.

fields.doc: steps between logs
Where else the metrics go: `[wandb(project="ablations"), tensorboard]`.

setting:precision.title: Precision
setting:precision.subtitle: precision
setting:precision.doc:
The dtype the forward and backward passes compute in, `compute`, and the format
the projections inside blocks multiply in, `matmuls` (a format of
bux.architecture.precision.matmuls: compute, mxfp8, mxfp8_2d, nvfp4).

`roles` gives a kind of projection a format of its own, `first` and `last` keep
residual branches at the ends of the model in compute, and of each projection's
GEMMs only `passes` multiply in the format, until a `switch`. Parameters stay
float32, and so do the optimizer's `moments` unless bfloat16, norm statistics,
router scores and top-k, recurrent states and the loss; gradients are summed over
rows in `reduce`. Unlike `mesh`, `layout`, `methods` and `compiler`, it is in the
run's id, all but `eval`.

fields.doc: the passes' dtype
The format the projections inside blocks multiply in, by name in bux.architecture.precision.matmuls: compute, mxfp8, mxfp8_2d or nvfp4.
a format by the kind of projection
attention's queries and gate (gqa, mla, csa, the indexer)
attention's keys and values
attention's output projection
MLPs, the shared experts' too
The routed experts, by a grouped GEMM: compute, mxfp8 or mxfp8_2d; none is `matmuls` where it is one of those, else compute, as no grouped GEMM takes nvfp4.
LatentMoE's projections to and from its latent
the recurrent mixers' projections, but the output

The residual branches outside any other at the start of the model that multiply in compute: a number of them, or a share of them, rounded up.
as `first`, the last ones before the first head

Evaluation multiplies as training does, or in compute.
The dtype the optimizer's moments are kept in between steps; they update in float32 (DeepSeek-V3's AdamW in bfloat16).
The dtype gradients are summed over the batch's rows in: compute, or float32 as Megatron's are, which a step sums once (methods.accumulate = unreduced).
What the MoE's exchanges send tokens to their experts in: compute, or MXFP8 (DeepSeek-V3's FP8 dispatch); what comes back, and gradients, go in compute.

setting:mesh.title: Mesh
setting:mesh.subtitle: mesh
setting:mesh.doc:
The device grid: a size for each of its six axes, whose product is the number
of devices a run takes. It lays them out the slowest links first: stage, data,
fsdp, context, expert, tensor, so that `tensor` stays inside a node. Which
dimensions each axis splits is the `layout`'s to say.

fields.doc: copies of the model; None: the devices left
pipeline stages
devices FSDP splits parameters over, rows too
devices a row's positions split over
devices the routed experts split over, rows too
devices heads, hidden units and the vocabulary split over

setting:layout.title: Layout
setting:layout.subtitle: layout
setting:layout.doc:
Which mesh axes each named dimension of parameters and activations splits over:
an axis, a list of them, or none. A dimension the axes' sizes do not divide stays
whole, and an axis of size 1 splits nothing, so the defaults only take effect as
`mesh` sizes their axes. `layout(stream=[context, tensor])` is sequence
parallelism.

3: FSDP splits parameters, gradients and the optimizer state; 1: it splits the optimizer state alone.

setting:methods.title: Methods
setting:methods.subtitle: methods
setting:methods.doc:
How each part that communicates is computed, by the name of a function in its
registry in bux.parallel.methods (the registries reference lists them), and how a
step takes its batch: in `microbatches`, its parameters gathered and its gradients
reduced how often. Another method is a function registered under a new name, not
a field.

fields.doc: Attention: auto (the fastest kernel that takes the call), xla, cudnn, tokamax; with `seq` over `context`, also ring and ulysses.
The MoE's experts: sorted or dense on each device's tokens; over the `expert` axis, all_gather, all_to_all, ragged_all_to_all, ragged_tokens or nccl_ep.

The picks a device of all_gather or the ragged MoE methods takes, or all_to_all sends each peer, a multiple of its own (of its share for a peer); what does not fit drops, which `dropped` reports. None: all that come.
The slices of each device's tokens that expert parallelism sends one after another, so that one's exchange runs beside another's experts.
nccl_ep's kernels on a GPU stream of their own, beside the compute stream's.

The linear attentions' recurrence: scan, all of a row's positions at once on each device; pass_state, with `seq` over `context`, each device's chunk of positions from the state the chunks before pass it (LASP-2).

What the backward pass of a recurrence by chunks reads of its chunks' states: kept from the forward pass, or computed again from its inputs, in a fourteenth of the memory and a fifth more time. The delta rule by cuDNN's kernels keeps only its inputs either way.
A repeat's passes: unroll, a module each, run in a row; scan, stacked into one module that a loop runs, where the passes can stack (else in a row).
A policy by name, or as data: remat(save=[attention], first=8). auto: the first of none, dots_attention, dots, save_attention and full whose step fits.
1f1b, zbh1, gpipe or circular: 1f1b runs where gpipe does, but in rounds and where a layer outside the pipelined repeat learns from the whole batch.
times a circular pipeline sends a microbatch round

The passes of the pipelined repeat each stage runs, first to last. None: under 1f1b and zbh1, the split that balances the stages' FLOPs, the embedding's on the first and the head's on the last (bux.train.stages); else as even as it goes.
How Muon reaches whole matrices: gspmd, on the shards the compiler gives; gather, each whole on every device that holds it; owner, each whole on one device.
How the loss takes a head's logits: chunks, a chunk of positions at a time, so that it never makes them all; logits, whole.
How TP's collectives meet the projections they feed: gspmd, as the compiler places them; chunked, each device's rows in chunks, so that a chunk's collective runs beside another's matmul.
the chunks of each device's rows, under chunked
The microbatches a step takes its batch in, adding up their gradients; under a pipeline, those it sends through its stages.

Each microbatch's forward beside the backward of the one before, a layer at a time, so that one's collectives run beside the other's compute. Off: it holds half a microbatch more and copies it across the loop, which pays only beside an exchange left exposed, as NCCL EP's with moe_stream (docs/parallelism/microbatches.md).

Where a step runs its layers more than once (microbatches, a pipeline's ticks), it casts and gathers the parameters FSDP splits once, or as each layer runs (ZeRO-3), which holds one layer's at a time.

How its microbatches' gradients add up: unreduced, each device's own reduced once a step; or reduced each microbatch. auto: unreduced where the devices along the rows' axes span more than one process (between hosts), and no layer learns from the whole batch as an MoE's router does; else reduced.
A step's new state takes the old one's memory: a lower peak, in fewer pieces.

setting:compiler.title: Compiler
setting:compiler.subtitle: compiler
setting:compiler.doc:
XLA's options for the training step: a preset's, by name in bux.train.xla, and
options of one's own over them. Like `mesh`, `layout` and `methods`, it changes
how a run computes, not what, and is not in the run's id.

fields.doc: XLA's own; o1, lhs, maxtext, collective_matmul

Over the preset's, as XLA_FLAGS writes them: "--xla_gpu_enable_triton_gemm=false --xla_gpu_threshold_for_windowed_einsum_mib=0". XLA's debug options, and jax's optimization_level and memory_fitting_level.
Where the step's gradient reductions start: early, each as its gradient is computed (bux.train.reorder, a pass over XLA's schedule); or where XLA puts them.

setting:search.title: Search
setting:search.subtitle: search
setting:search.doc:
How a run with dimensions (`uniform`, `log_uniform`, `int_uniform`, `choice`)
is searched: `trials` points, each a run of its own, proposed by `method`, ranked
by the run's `objective`. Each run of a sweep is a search of its own, so
``attn.num_kv_heads = 1 | 4`` with ``optimizer.lr = log_uniform(1e-4, 1e-2)`` tunes
the learning rate of each attention apart, and compares them at their best.

`bux launch` trains the trials side by side, a GPU group each, and proposes the
next as one ends. The search keeps its trials in its own directory, so a search
launched again goes on where it stopped, and one given more trials adds them.
